# Part A: Data Importing

Ensure the package `readr` (part of the `tidyverse`) and `here` are loaded, then import the plastic waste dataset using relative paths.

```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(here)

# Import the macroplastics csv file using relative paths
plastics_df <- read_csv(here("data", "theme6_plastic_waste.csv"))

# Inspect the imported data frame
head(plastics_df)
```

# Part B: Identifying Untidy Data

Review the two tables representing household energy biomass usage:

### Table A (Wide / Untidy)
| Household | Charcoal_Kg_Day1 | Charcoal_Kg_Day2 | Firewood_Kg_Day1 | Firewood_Kg_Day2 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| HH01 | 2.5 | 3.0 | 5.0 | 4.5 |
| HH02 | 1.0 | 1.2 | 8.0 | 7.5 |

### Table B (Long / Tidy)
| Household | Fuel_Type | Day | Amount_Kg |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| HH01 | Charcoal | Day 1 | 2.5 |
| HH01 | Charcoal | Day 2 | 3.0 |
| HH01 | Firewood | Day 1 | 5.0 |
| HH01 | Firewood | Day 2 | 4.5 |
| HH02 | Charcoal | Day 1 | 1.0 |
| HH02 | Charcoal | Day 2 | 1.2 |
| HH02 | Firewood | Day 1 | 8.0 |
| HH02 | Firewood | Day 2 | 7.5 |

# Discussion Questions
1. Why is **Table B** tidy and **Table A** untidy?
2. If you wanted to calculate the average fuel amount used by each household, which table format makes this query simpler?
